title: Router::handle reserves verb names that protocol.md does not list
body:
`Envelope` in `channel.rs` reads `hello`, `focus`, `status` and `panes` as optional fields, and `Router::handle`, 90 lines, checks them in that order before `to`. So `{"to":"code","focus":{..}}` is taken as a focus request, and `{"to":"code","status":{}}` answers "malformed: missing field state". On the client, `parse` in `decade-channel` checks `welcome`, `error` and `panes` before treating a key as a verb, so a pane verb named `error` from another client reads as a decade message. `docs/protocol.md` does not say these names are reserved. A client may also send `hello` again and change its name and pane; the doc does not say so either.

## Proposal

`handle` first splits on whether `to` is present: with it, forward the single remaining key; without it, dispatch the decade verb. Each branch becomes a method. `protocol.md` lists `hello`, `focus`, `status`, `panes`, `welcome` and `error` as reserved and says what a second `hello` does.
close_reason: Landed in 2d4b451. handle splits on to into forward and command, and decade refuses a pane verb with a reserved name, so decade-channel's parse needed no change. from is reserved along with the six names in the proposal, because forward writes it. A line without to must now hold exactly one key, where extra keys used to be ignored. docs/protocol.md lists the reserved names and describes a second hello.
